headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: broad-write, browser-capable transformers can ingest and act on spring-integration-samples outputs without default isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A has no shared channel or input surface documented, but Profile B can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout, so if A’s outputs are copied into B’s workspace they can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into files or stdin consumed by agent_b
IF agent_b parses agent_a-generated text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep agent_a and agent_b on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent_a output into agent_b prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor
Review agent_b inputs before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B has broad network egress and filesystem access, while Agent A is docs-only with no network egress. If they share a workspace, B can read and transmit files that A produced or that contain sensitive user content. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default document-processing setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF sensitive documents are placed in that shared workspace and agent_b processes them
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Block agent_b from reading agent_a output folders
Route sensitive files through a redaction step first
Disable network egress for agent_b during sensitive runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can execute shell commands, install packages, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses; Agent A is a sample integration repo with no concurrency controls or locking documented. If both operate on the same directory, B’s mutable actions can overwrite or corrupt A’s artifacts. Because shared-write coordination is not shown, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same directory
IF agent_b installs packages or rewrites files while agent_a is generating artifacts
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Snapshot the workspace before agent_b runs
Use file locks or a job queue
Mount agent_a outputs read-only for agent_b

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s pipeline API and browser/shell capabilities make it likely to act on upstream text, while Agent A is a sample integration source that could supply instructions or facts. If B treats A’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated documents. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as a trusted pipeline input
IF agent_b emits downstream artifacts or actions based on unverified agent_a content
mitigations: Insert a verification step before agent_b acts
Require source citations for all claims from agent_a
Log and diff agent_a outputs before reuse
Disable automatic execution of generated instructions
Use human approval for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented for either open-source profile, and agent_a touches no data classes. Agent B handles multimodal data and can egress broadly, but without a stated regulated data class or residency constraint, the compliance risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through agent_b
IF a residency or retention policy is imposed externally on the pair
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention and deletion rules
Restrict agent_b network destinations
Add a data-class gate before processing
